t.7.5.2: He had a daughter named Devavatī, like a second Śrī. He gave her in marriage to Sukeśa according to dharma, just as Dakṣa gave Śrī.
t.7.5.1: Seeing that the Rākṣasa Sukeśa was righteous and had obtained a boon, a Gandharva named Grāmaṇī, equal in splendour to Viśvāvasu,
t.7.5.3: Having obtained him as her beloved husband, whose sovereignty had been won through the granting of a boon, Devavatī was as delighted as a penniless man who has come upon wealth.
t.7.5.4: United with her, that night-roamer shone like a great elephant come forth from Añjana together with a she-elephant.
t.7.5.5: O Rāghava, Sukeśa, lord of the Rākṣasas, begot on Devavatī three Rākṣasa sons equal to the three-eyed god: Mālyavant, Sumāli, and Māli, the foremost of the mighty.
t.7.5.6: Unshaken like the three worlds, they stood like the three sacred fires; exceedingly fierce like the three mantras, the three were like three dreadful diseases.
t.7.5.7: The three sons of Sukeśa, whose splendor equaled that of the three sacred fires, grew to great strength there, like diseases left neglected.
t.7.5.8: They, the brothers, having learned of their father's obtaining of boons and of his great sovereignty, then went to Meru with firm resolve to practise austerities.
t.7.5.9: O best of kings, those rākṣasas, taking up severe vows, practised terrible austerities that struck fear into all beings.
t.7.5.10: With austerities hard to perform on earth, joined with truthfulness, uprightness and self-restraint, they scorched the three worlds together with their gods, asuras and humans.
t.7.5.11: Then the mighty four-faced lord, seated in his excellent celestial chariot, addressed the sons of Sukeśa and said, "I am the giver of boons."
t.7.5.12: Recognizing Brahmā, the giver of boons, surrounded by the hosts of gods together with Indra, they all spoke with joined palms, trembling like trees.
t.7.5.13: O god, propitiated by our austerity, if you would grant us a boon, may we be invincible, slayers of our enemies, and likewise long-lived and mighty, ever devoted to one another.
t.7.5.14: Having said to the sons of Sukeśa, "So it shall be," the lord Brahmā, who is affectionate toward brāhmaṇas, departed for Brahmaloka.
t.7.5.15: Then, O Rāma, having obtained the boon, all those night-rangers, utterly fearless because of the granting of the boon, began to harass the gods and the Asuras.
t.7.5.16: Being slain by them, the gods, together with the hosts of seers and with the Cāraṇas, found no protector, like men dwelling in hell.
t.7.5.17: Then, O best of the Raghus, those rākṣasas, having come together in great delight, spoke to Viśvakarman, the imperishable, foremost among craftsmen.
t.7.5.19: Taking refuge on Himavant, on Meru, or on Mandara, let a great dwelling be built for us, like the abode of Maheśvara.
t.7.5.18: You alone are the builder of dwellings for the gods, fashioned as their hearts desire; so now, O wise one, build a dwelling for us as well.
t.7.5.20: Then the mighty-armed Viśvakarmā told those Rākṣasas of a dwelling place for them, like Amarāvatī of Śakra.
t.7.5.22: A city named Laṅkā, thirty yojanas in extent, with golden ramparts and gateways, was built by me at the command of Śakra.
t.7.5.21: On the shore of the southern ocean stands a mountain named Trikūṭa. On the middle peak of that mountain, which resembles a cloud, is hard to reach even for birds, and is sheer on all four sides as if cut by a chisel…
t.7.5.23: Dwell in that city, O invincible ones, O best of Rākṣasas, as the heaven-dwellers together with Indra dwell on reaching Amarāvatī.
t.7.5.24: Having reached the fortress of Laṅkā, surrounded by many Rākṣasas, you will become unassailable by your enemies, O destroyers of foes.
t.7.5.26: Having obtained Laṅkā, with its strong ramparts and moats, surrounded by hundreds of golden houses, those night-roamers joyfully took their pleasure there.
t.7.5.25: Having heard the words of Viśvakarman, O Rāma, those Rākṣasas then went with thousands of followers to that city of Laṅkā and dwelt there.
t.7.5.27: There was a Gandharvī named Narmadā, flourishing in many virtues. She had three daughters, equal in radiance to Dhī, Śrī and Kīrti.
t.7.5.28: Delighted, she, who was herself no rākṣasī, gave those maidens, whose faces shone like the full moon, to those rākṣasas in order of their seniority.
t.7.5.29: To the three lords of the Rākṣasas, three illustrious Gandharva maidens were given in marriage by their mother, under the constellation whose presiding deity is Bhaga.
t.7.5.30: And those sons of Sukeśa, O Rāma, O lord, having taken wives, sported with their consorts as the immortals do with the Apsarases.
t.7.5.31: There, the wife of Mālyavat was the beautiful Sundarī by name. Learn of the offspring he begot upon her.
t.7.5.33: Sumālin too had a wife whose face was like the full moon, Ketumatī by name, who was dearer to him than life itself.
t.7.5.32: Vajramuṣṭi, Virūpākṣa, the rākṣasa Durmukha, Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, and likewise Matta and Unmatta were born; and of Sundarī, O Rāma, there was also born a beautiful daughter, Analā.
t.7.5.34: O great king, hear from me in due order of the offspring that the night-roamer Sumālī begot upon Ketumatī.
t.7.5.35: Prahasta along with the Akampanas, Vikaṭa, Kālakārmuka, Dhūmrākṣa, and then Daṇḍa, and Supārśva of mighty strength.
t.7.5.36: Saṃhrādi, Praghasa, and the Rākṣasa Bhāsakarṇa, and Rākā, Puṣpotkaṭā, sweet-smiling Kaikasī, and Kumbhīnasī: these are known as the offspring of Sumāli.
t.7.5.37: Mālī's wife was a Gandharvī named Vasudā, endowed with beauty, lotus-petal-eyed and fair-eyed, comparable to the finest of Yakṣīs.
t.7.5.38: O lord, hear from me, O Rāghava, as I relate it, of the offspring that Sumāli's younger brother begot in her.
t.7.5.39: Anala and Anila, Hara and Saṃpāti: these night-roaming rākṣasas, the sons of Mālī, became the ministers of Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.7.5.41: Roaming the world like the wind, hard to approach, and in battle like Death itself, resolute and intent, they were exceedingly arrogant because of the boon granted to them, and were ever the disruptors of sacrificial rites.
t.7.5.40: Then those three bulls among the rākṣasas, surrounded by night-roamers and by hundreds of sons, and proud of their strength and valor, oppressed the gods together with Indra, as well as the ṛṣis, nāgas and dānavas.
